After calling newEmergencyOracle("test") as the jojoTeam address, the owner of the newly created EmergencyOracle contract is msg.sender in the reference but jojoTeam in the bug; reading the owner() getter on the new oracle reveals the divergence.
After calling newEmergencyOracle("test") as jojoTeam, the owner of the new EmergencyOracle is msg.sender in the reference but jojoTeam in the bug, observable via the owner() getter on the new oracle.

Invoking newEmergencyOracle('test') as an address that is not the jojoTeam should revert due to the onlyJojoTeam modifier, but the buggy version silently succeeds because the modifier is triggered after the constructor call; the reference sees 'owner' as msg.sender (the caller) while the bug sees it as address(0) (jojoTeam) and the test can observe that the reference reverts and the bug does not.

After calling newEmergencyOracle('test') as the jojoTeam address, the reference sets the owner of the new EmergencyOracle to msg.sender, while the bug sets it to jojoTeam; reading the owner() getter on the new oracle via a getter function on C reveals the divergence.
When a non-owner calls newEmergencyOracle, the reference reverts due to onlyJojoTeam modifier, but the buggy version allows the call and succeeds.
